name: FramerD
tagline: MIT Media Lab's distributed frame database for knowledge bases, scripted in a Scheme dialect.
description: FramerD was a distributed object database built at the MIT Media Laboratory by Ken Haase for knowledge bases made of frames: objects with many slots that point at each other, as in semantic networks and agent systems. It stored millions of pointer-heavy frames in file pools and indexes that could be spread across networked servers, and shipped FDScript, a Scheme-based language for querying and building web interfaces over the data. Development moved from MIT to SourceForge with support from the startup beingmeta; the last release, 2.6.1, came out in January 2005. Its ideas continued in beingmeta's Kno platform. Today it is of historical interest for anyone studying frame-based knowledge representation.
statusNote: Last release 2.6.1 in January 2005; framerd.org now hosts unrelated content. Its architecture continued in beingmeta's Kno project.

scale.notes: Pools of frames could be split across networked servers; sized for millions of frames on 2000s hardware.

strengths: Built for pointer-intensive frame and semantic-network data
Frames carry arbitrary slots without up-front schema design
Scheme scripting language integrated with the store
Open GPL source remains a reference for frame-system storage
weaknesses: Unmaintained for two decades; builds target 2000s toolchains
No ACID transactions or modern replication
Original website lost; documentation survives only in archives
useCases: Reading the source behind beingmeta's later Kno platform
notIdealFor: Modern knowledge graphs (use RDF or property-graph stores)
